doc.title: Eric Alexander interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010

chapter: Coming up: Indiana and William Paterson
title: Parents, leaving for New York, and getting into William Paterson
summary: His parents did not know his dedication until later; after he proposed Greenwich Village, they pushed him to William Paterson, where Rufus Reid admitted him and Harold Mabern was his first instructor.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You had mentioned yesterday your father listening to you practice, and can’t you play a song all the way through or something. Did you win them over, your parents, with your dedication?

I don’t think my parents really ever knew until later how dedicated I was. Because I think the proof is really in the pudding. And I wasn’t living with them. I was far away from home when this started to happen to me. You know I had periods of time in high school where I would prepare very diligently for a saxophone recital, classical saxophone, I would learn a piece and make big strides and have some effective practice moments. So they knew I was talented. You know all of the teachers would tell them, oh your son’s very talented. And my parents are musical as well so they could hear it. But I don’t think they — I don’t know what they thought. I’m sure they were a little bit uneasy about, not when I went to Indiana University, they were fine with that. It was at the end of that first year when I said I’m going to New York, I’m leaving Indiana. I want to go right to where everything is happening. I might not even go to school, Dad. I might just go try to figure out how to play in Greenwich Village. And another one of his classic lines, he said, “If you do that, kid, you’ll be selling your ass within a week.” So I think at that point they sort of rallied. You know my parents are divorced but they joined forces and said, “Look, you’re not dropping out of school. If you want to go to the New York area you better find someplace where you can get a degree and at least be somewhere safe while you’re pursuing this cockamamie idea.” So I found William Paterson — a friend of mine and I found William Paterson college. I don’t even know how we found it. It’s really serendipitous. I don’t know how these things fall into place, but it was sort of a last ditch, it was the last place we could possibly apply to in the late part of the spring semester. And we sent audition tapes and Rufus Reid who was the head of the department heard our audition tapes and, for whatever reason, even though they weren’t very good, said yeah, these guys have some talent, I’m letting them in, they really want this. We were begging and pleading. And the next semester I get to William Paterson and the first instructor I had in the small group ensemble was Harold Mabern. And really the rest is history.
